extracted.intended_audience: UVA alumni and general readers interested in comedy, memoirs, and Tina Fey
extracted.subtask_description: A short magazine review of Tina Fey's memoir Bossypants that highlights her comedic techniques, tone, character work, and workplace/bossing advice as evidence of why she succeeded. Useful for readers studying humor, comedic voice, or memoir craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sympathy as a comedic tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Fey uses sympathy as a comedic tool, often finding humor in moments of cultural misunderstanding, asking us to see how both sides could be right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empathy/sympathy to frame jokes so the audience can recognize multiple perspectives; humor arises from acknowledging competing viewpoints rather than simply mocking one side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create complicated characters defined by dueling motivations
rubrics_metrics.description: Her characters are complicated, defined by dueling motivations, resulting in funny, honest sketches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write characters with conflicting desires or impulses; those internal tensions generate authentic, funny situations and sustain sketch comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance serious insights with incisive wit (frequent tone changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fey changes her tone frequently, and serious insights are quickly balanced by incisive wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary tone within a piece—alternate between sincerity and sharp humor to keep writing dynamic and to let insight land without undercutting the joke or the sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be both ambitious and self-deprecating
rubrics_metrics.description: She’s our modern comedienne, both ambitious and self-deprecating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine confidence/ambition with self-mockery to make comedic persona relatable and multi-dimensional rather than one-note brashness or false humility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coin neologisms to capture a specific comic feeling ('blorft')
rubrics_metrics.description: "'Blorft' is an adjective I just made up... It means 'completely overwhelmed but proceeding as if everything is fine and reacting to the stress with the torpor of a possum.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invent precise, funny words or turns of phrase to name complex feelings or states—these can become memorable comedic hooks and encapsulate character voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use literalness/precision in comedic phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Example anecdote: 'Not figuratively. Literally.' (the joke hinges on literal vs. figurative interpretation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punchlines can come from choosing literal wording or calling out the literal meaning; precision and playful contradiction of expectations sharpen the humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mine humor from cultural misunderstanding and industry observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: 'Only in comedy, by the way, does a white girl from the suburbs count as diversity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observations about institutions, culture, or industry norms (including ironic or self-aware critiques) as sources of comedic commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical bossing: hire talented people and then get out of their way
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases being a good boss means hiring talented people and then getting out of their way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a creative leader, prioritize talent selection and give writers/performers autonomy rather than micromanaging; this supports better creative output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workplace presentation advice for women: no pigtails, no tube tops, cry sparingly
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a woman and you bought this book for practical tips... No pigtails, no tube tops. Cry sparingly. (Some people say 'Never let them see you cry.' I say, if you’re so mad you could just cry, then cry. It terrifies everyone.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical, stylistic workplace tips about appearance and emotional display—use intentional presentation and strategic emotional expression as tools for professional navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle sexism/other '-isms' by asking if the person blocks your goals
rubrics_metrics.description: When faced with sexism, ageism, or lookism... ask yourself: 'Is this person in between me and what I want to do?' If the answer is no, ignore it and move on. Your energy is better used doing your work and outpacing people that way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate discriminatory behavior by its practical impact on your objectives; prioritize actions that advance your work rather than engaging every slight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative, late-night rewrite culture and dedicated staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Recounting a rewrite: writers fell asleep talking; other writers were just sitting politely, awaiting further instruction. That is a dedicated staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate a collaborative writers' room willing to do intensive rewrites and to follow the lead of producers/writers; dedication and patience among staff support show-quality results.
